newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates up on repo sentiment, seen lower.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates up on repo sentiment, seen lower.

text.p: Indian call money rates opened higher on Tuesday at 8.00-9.00 percent against the previous close of 6.00-6.50 percent, dealers said.

Some of the major lenders were quoting rates in the region of 9.25-9.50 percent, a dealer said. "But it seems to be sentiment-driven quotes, as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mopped 48 billion rupees in the Monday's repo auction," he said.
The net outflow on account of repo auction was negligible as the repurchase of previous repo was 37.1 billion rupees.
"The rates should stabilise to 6.0 percent levels towards the close, as the demand will ease," a state-run bank dealer said.
"The rates will rule below 6.0 percent for the rest of the fortnight as the next repo auction will attract less bidders," he said.
The securities market is expected to remain subdued on higher call levels, with some selling pressure, a dealer said.
